q: It is 16:30 at the base in Lefkas. The technician hands you the form and says he will start with the engine. How do you run the walk-round?

A request for the deck re-cored before you sail

Ask for the roller only; a loose cleat and a stopper are the base's wear
Tighten the cleat from below yourself and note the roller and the stopper

Switch the instruments on — a wind reading means the masthead is fine

q: Wednesday, under way, the steering feels like this. What do you do?
a: Call the base now and motor gently to the nearest harbour to meet their technician
o: Carry on and tell the base at check-out; the play is on the form
Open the binnacle and tighten the cables yourself under way
Carry on under autopilot so that the wheel takes no load
why: Play that grows with a knock is a cable or quadrant going; the base fixes it in harbour before it parts at sea.

fig.title: Wednesday, 11:00
lines: Half a turn of play before the rudder moves
A knock under the cockpit floor
Check-in: 'steering adjusted, play 1/8 turn'

q: Thursday evening at anchor, your crew want the bimini left up for the morning sun. What do you do?
a: Take the panels off, fold the bimini and lash it — it is not built for that wind
o: Leave it up, with a line tied in place of the missing strap
Leave it up; it was noted at check-in, so damage is the base's
Take the side panels off and leave the top up for the morning
why: A bimini up in 30 kn gusts tears or bends its frame; damage from your week is yours, noted strap or not.

fig.title: Thursday, 18:00
lines: Forecast: gusts 30 kn overnight
Bimini up, side panels on
Check-in form: 'bimini: one strap missing'

q: Thursday, 28 miles from the base, your morning look at the rig finds this. What do you do?
a: Call the base now; stay, or motor back sails down, as they decide — not sail on it
o: Sail back reefed, on the tack that takes the load off that shroud
Tape the strands and sail back early, before the wind arrives
Leave it for Friday's check-out; one more day on it is fine
why: Broken strands mean the wire is going; with a beat ahead the rig must not be loaded — the base sends a rigger or agrees a return.
